messages:
maya: drafting a concise playbook for a zero-touch onprem onramp. want to align on netops preflight and upgrade expectations.

sam: field asks so far: clear IP reservation examples, egress NAT guidance, and a non-disruptive upgrade path. customers keep pressing for a safe patch flow.

olivia: also include explicit guidance for when customers manage the LB vs when we provide ingress. that changes DNS and firewall requirements.

jack: does the operator assume hostNetwork? some enterprises forbid hostNetwork for security reasons.

maya: propose two options in the doc: A) operator without hostNetwork (requires port-forward or sidecar) and B) hostNetwork with elevated privileges. surface tradeoffs.

emily: netops preflight list I want: sample CIDR reservation, BGP handshake sample (if used), cert distribution notes, and a small connectivity smoke test.

sam: agree. also let's publish a tiny preflight script the field can run and paste into a ticket. basic checks: metadata access, LB port reachability, iperf/throughput test. keep it readable.

olivia: script should be read-only, print remediation steps, and include a kubectl snippet to assert operator CR health.

maya: noted. product decision around upgrades: default to manual upgrades for GA, with an opt-in auto-upgrade toggle for customers who want it. reduces early risk.

jack: manual default makes sense. include a documented rolling upgrade procedure: label canary nodes, deploy canary operator, watch logs, verify KV cache warmup before full roll. keep steps short.

emily: for customer-managed networking provide paste-ready BGP templates for Cisco/Arista and a minimal NAT example so netops can copy/paste.

maya: add fallback: if catalog access fails, runtime falls back to a pinned local model bundle. call out minimum storage and checksum validation steps.

sam: proposed launch criteria: 1) preflight script and smoke-tests documented, 2) upgrade doc + rollback playbook, 3) three reference validations across topologies (isolated on-prem, VPC+NAT, BGP-connected), 4) support runbook + sample BGP configs.

olivia: also require audit logs for peering events and cert rotations for compliance customers.

jack: add a troubleshooting matrix for common failures: DNS misconfig, MTU mismatch, TLS/KMS handshake issues — one-liner causes and first checks.

maya: I'll draft the playbook this week and post a link. tagging @deploy-bot to open a QA ticket for reference validations.

deploy-bot: [automation] created ticket PROD-ONRAMP-542 assigned to sam for "reference validations: zero-touch onramp" due 2024-06-05.

emily: once QA ticket is live we can schedule field validation with ACME Corp next week.

maya: timeline in the doc: draft by Fri, internal review Mon, field validation Wed. anything else to add?

sam: include expected canary SLAs (p50/p95 latency bounds, error budget) and telemetry hooks we need from runtime to detect regressions.

olivia: include RBAC examples so customers can restrict operator impersonation; show minimal policies.

maya: will include both. thanks all.
